title: UI/UX
blurb: Usability heuristics, accessibility, layout and interaction design for engineers.

quiz.question: What is the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum contrast ratio for normal body text?
quiz.explanation: AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and UI components; AAA raises normal text to 7:1.

quiz.question: Hick's law says that…
options: Decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices
Bigger targets are slower to hit
quiz.explanation: More options means slower decisions, so progressive disclosure and sensible defaults help. Fitts's law is about target size and distance.

quiz.question: Which is the best practice for form error messages?
options: Show a generic error at the top only
Show specific, inline messages next to the field, explaining how to fix it, and keep the user's input
Use colour alone to signal errors
quiz.explanation: Specific inline errors (linked with aria-describedby), preserved input, and more than colour alone make forms usable and accessible.

quiz.question: Why should focus outlines not be removed with outline: none?
options: Keyboard users rely on a visible focus indicator to know where they are
They are required for mouse users
quiz.explanation: Removing focus styles breaks keyboard navigation (WCAG 2.4.7). Use :focus-visible to style focus for keyboard users without showing it on mouse clicks.

quiz.question: A good minimum touch target size is around…
options: 24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.2 AA), with 44–48 px recommended
quiz.explanation: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets a 24×24 CSS px minimum; Apple recommends 44 pt and Material Design 48 dp for comfortable tapping.

problems.title: Audit a sign-up form
problems.prompt: List the UX and accessibility issues to check on a sign-up form before launch.
problems.solution: Visible <label>s (placeholders aren't labels), correct input types and autocomplete attributes, minimal required fields, inline specific errors announced to screen readers, password rules shown up front with a show-password toggle, logical tab order and visible focus, sufficient contrast, touch targets of at least 24 px, a clear primary action, and no CAPTCHA that blocks assistive tech.

problems.title: Design empty, loading and error states
problems.prompt: A dashboard table can be empty, loading or fail to load. Describe each state.
problems.solution: Loading: a skeleton matching the table layout (avoid layout shift), announced politely to screen readers. Empty: explain why it's empty and offer the next action ("Create your first project"). Error: plain-language message, what happened and a retry button, keeping any data already loaded. All three use the same container so the layout stays stable.
